findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I'm approving this RED. The attestation shows the exact command ran and failed with exit 1. It wasn't a signal and didn't time out (20.1s of a 180s budget). The expected literal "Unmapped-case refusal must name the exact case identity" appears in the full, untruncated stdout. The proof follows the scenario. Its When step is a public `proof observe-bounded-delivery --json --no-input` request against a built disposable distribution whose shipped profile omits one mapping. The project census is left unchanged. Its Then step is the actor-visible refusal message. Before the failing check, these assertions already passed: exit code 2, status 'refused', and authority 'execution-only'. So the CLI ran, refused before execution, and the failure lands at the intended missing behavior: the message says "Unsupported or unmapped delivery case; review a complete shipped mapping" but doesn't name the omitted case. The failure is not caused by syntax, imports, the fixture or build, configuration or infrastructure. I can't recompute the source fingerprint; I'm treating it as binding the declared targets.

The case-name check is too weak. `message.includes(distribution.missingCase)` would also pass if the GREEN refusal listed every case ID in the shipped profile or feature census (for example, an 'expected cases: …' dump). That would not name the specific unmapped case. Strengthen it before GREEN: assert that the message names the missing ID and none of the other 36 mapped case IDs, or check a structured error field that carries only the unmapped identity.

Several assertions in `expectNamedUnmappedCase` haven't run yet: the `/review.*complete.*mapping/` match, the report_path-absent check, and the diagnostic.log check that the clone-preparation stage never ran. They come after the line that failed. If diagnostic.log isn't written on a pre-execution refusal, `readFileSync` will throw instead of asserting, which would be a wrong-reason failure at GREEN. Confirm the refusal path always writes that diagnostic, or guard the read with an `existsSync` check that states what it expects.

The test removes the first profile row (`profile.cases.shift()`) and checks that the profile has exactly 37 rows. That ties the control to one fixed case. If the shipped profile's ordering changes, the test still works, but only one position is ever tested. That's acceptable for this scenario.

The attested parent Node is v24.3.0, while the plan pins v24.18.1. This doesn't affect this RED, because the observer runs under Bun 1.3.14 and the test makes no tool-identity assertions. Expect a mismatch if the complete-observation fixture is run in the same environment.
